t: The battle was the first American offensive in the Central Pacific and the first time in the Pacific War that a United States amphibious landing met serious, well prepared Japanese opposition.

A neap tide left only about 3 feet of water over the reef, so most landing craft could not cross it and the Marines had to wade ashore or be carried in by tracked LVTs, half of which were knocked out on the first day.
Of the 3,636 Japanese in the garrison, only one officer and sixteen enlisted men survived, and only 129 of the 1,200 Korean labourers.
dyk: Marine cameramen filmed the dead on the beaches at Tarawa, and the decision on whether to release the footage was deferred to President Franklin D. Roosevelt, who approved it.
ev: Colonel Evans Carlson's raid on Makin Island makes the Japanese command aware of the vulnerability of the Gilbert Islands
The 6th Yokosuka Special Naval Landing Force reinforces Betio under Rear Admiral Tomonari
The Joint Chiefs of Staff direct Admiral Nimitz to plan an offensive in the Gilberts, and Rear Admiral Shibazaki relieves Tomonari
Marines land on the north shore of Betio under fire, with the tide too low for most landing craft to cross the reef
A Japanese counterattack at night and in the early hours is broken up, and Betio is declared secure on 23 November
A New York Times editorial warns that future assaults may cost even more, after public protest at the losses
The 2nd Marine Division is withdrawn, and Nimitz launches the Marshalls campaign ten weeks after Tarawa

f.date: 20–23 November 1943; the landing was at 09:10 on 20 November and Betio was declared secure at 13:30 on 23 November
f.place: Betio, the largest island of Tarawa Atoll in the Gilbert Islands, now part of the Republic of Kiribati but then a Japanese-occupied British colony
f.sides: The United States, under Admiral Raymond Spruance, Admiral Richmond Kelly Turner and Major General Julian C. Smith, with the 2nd Marine Division (roughly 12,000 Marines on Tarawa); Japan, under Rear Admiral Keiji Shibazaki, with a garrison counted at 3,636 or at 4,500 defenders, besides about 1,200 Korean labourers
f.outcome: American victory: Betio was taken and almost the whole garrison killed, with 4,690 of the island's defenders dead and 3,166 casualties in the 2nd Marine Division.
